name: Optic nerve
synonyms: cranial nerve II (intracranial and orbital segments)
contextNote: Schematic anterior visual/olfactory pathway representation. Retained origin/size/waypoints are custom teaching coordinates and do not validate individual nerve fila, retinal layers, chiasmal fibres, orbital/canal geometry or patient anatomy. Named level membership is teaching/navigation metadata and has not been validated as a literal intersection of every displayed transverse section. The clinical text describes possible associations, not diagnostic rules.
modality: Special somatic sensory: retinal output from the ipsilateral eye before chiasmal partial crossing
origin: Retinal ganglion cells of the ipsilateral eye
target: Optic chiasm and continuation into optic tracts; no synapse in the chiasm
decussation: No crossing within the optic nerve. Nasal retinal fibres cross at the chiasm; temporal retinal fibres remain ipsilateral.
function: The optic nerve contains retinal ganglion-cell axons from one eye before the chiasm. It is developmentally a CNS pathway, with oligodendrocyte myelin posterior to the lamina cribrosa and a meningeal sheath. It conveys retinal output for vision and reflex/circadian pathways; it does not yet encode one contralateral binocular hemifield.

clinical.findings: Can cause monocular acuity/color/field loss and a relative afferent pupillary defect when asymmetric. Patterns depend on inflammatory, ischemic, compressive or other causes.
Raised intracranial pressure can cause optic-disc swelling through the continuous nerve-sheath subarachnoid space; disc swelling also has other causes.

refs: Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 465-475 and 914-915 (PDF pp. 491-501 and 940-941), Figures 11.8-11.15
Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 395-402 (PDF pp. 421-428), Figures 10.4-10.9; territories and collaterals vary

afferent: Retinal ganglion-cell axons from the ipsilateral eye
efferent: Continuation through optic chiasm into optic tracts, with retinal projections ultimately reaching LGN and extrageniculate targets

bloodSupply: Optic-nerve head: mainly short posterior ciliary circulation; posterior orbital/canalicular nerve: ophthalmic/pial branches; intracranial segment: small carotid/ACA-related branches. Supply is segment-specific.

name: Optic chiasm (chiasmatic crossing)
contextNote: Schematic anterior visual/olfactory pathway representation. Retained origin/size/waypoints are custom teaching coordinates and do not validate individual nerve fila, retinal layers, chiasmal fibres, orbital/canal geometry or patient anatomy. Named level membership is teaching/navigation metadata and has not been validated as a literal intersection of every displayed transverse section. The clinical text describes possible associations, not diagnostic rules.
function: The optic chiasm is a flattened midline partial crossing above the pituitary/sella and below the hypothalamus. Nasal retinal fibres cross while temporal retinal fibres remain ipsilateral, reorganizing each optic tract to represent the contralateral binocular visual hemifield. There is no synaptic relay here; Wilbrand's knee should not be taught as a verified normal human fibre loop.

afferent: Retinal ganglion-cell axons via both optic nerves
efferent: Optic tracts; retinal fibres to hypothalamic circadian targets also leave the anterior visual pathway

bloodSupply: Small branches of carotid/superior hypophyseal and ACA/anterior communicating systems; contributions vary.

clinical.findings: Can cause bitemporal field loss with variable asymmetry; compression from below often affects superior temporal fields first, but other patterns occur.
Optic-nerve loss in one eye plus a temporal defect in the other suggests nerve/chiasm involvement; it does not require a normal Wilbrand knee or prove one specific mass.

refs: Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 465-475 and 914-915 (PDF pp. 491-501 and 940-941), Figures 11.8-11.15
Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 395-402 (PDF pp. 421-428), Figures 10.4-10.9; territories and collaterals vary
Horton JC (1997), Wilbrand's knee of the primate optic chiasm is an artefact of monocular enucleation. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9440188/

name: Optic tract
synonyms: optic tract (chiasm to lateral geniculate nucleus)
contextNote: Schematic anterior visual/olfactory pathway representation. Retained origin/size/waypoints are custom teaching coordinates and do not validate individual nerve fila, retinal layers, chiasmal fibres, orbital/canal geometry or patient anatomy. Named level membership is teaching/navigation metadata and has not been validated as a literal intersection of every displayed transverse section. The clinical text describes possible associations, not diagnostic rules.
modality: Special somatic sensory: contralateral binocular visual hemifield and retinal reflex/orienting projections
origin: Optic chiasm: ipsilateral temporal plus contralateral nasal retinal fibres
target: LGN, with additional pretectal/superior-collicular retinal projections
decussation: No crossing in the optic tract; partial retinal crossing has occurred at the chiasm.
function: Each optic tract continues posterolaterally from the chiasm around the diencephalic/cerebral-peduncular region and carries the contralateral visual hemifield from both eyes. Most fibres reach the LGN; others serve pretectal and collicular functions. The retinohypothalamic circadian projection is a separate retinal pathway, not an obligatory tract-to-SCN relay.

clinical.findings: Can cause contralateral homonymous field loss, often incongruous, but congruity alone does not reliably locate every lesion.
An asymmetric optic-tract lesion may cause a contralateral relative afferent pupillary defect. This is distinct from the Riddoch phenomenon, which concerns residual motion perception.

refs: Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 465-475 and 914-915 (PDF pp. 491-501 and 940-941), Figures 11.8-11.15
Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 395-402 (PDF pp. 421-428), Figures 10.4-10.9; territories and collaterals vary

afferent: Retinal ganglion-cell axons after partial chiasmal crossing
efferent: LGN for geniculostriate vision; pretectal and superior-collicular targets for reflex/orienting pathways

bloodSupply: Variable anterior choroidal and proximal carotid/PCA-related branches.
